facts.statement: Eotyrannus is a genus of tyrannosauroid theropod dinosaur meaning "dawn tyrant".
facts.quote: Eotyrannus (meaning "dawn tyrant") is a genus of tyrannosauroid theropod dinosaur

facts.statement: The fossil was found in a plant debris clay bed and described by Stephen Hutt and colleagues in early 2001.
facts.quote: found in a plant debris clay bed, were described by Stephen Hutt and colleagues in early 2001

facts.statement: Local collector Gavin Leng found a claw in 1995 and brought it to Steve Hutt, leading to the excavation of the site.
facts.quote: In 1995, local collector Gavin Leng brought a claw he had found along the coastline to Steve Hutt

facts.statement: The specific epithet of Eotyrannus honors Gavin Leng, the collector who discovered the initial claw.
facts.quote: Eventually in 2001, Eotyrannus was given its name along with its specific epithet in honour of Mr. Leng

facts.statement: A detailed monograph describing the specimen was published in the journal PeerJ in 2022.
facts.quote: The monograph was eventually published in the journal PeerJ in 2022

facts.statement: Eotyrannus lived in the Early Cretaceous Wessex Formation on the southwest coast of the Isle of Wight, United Kingdom.
facts.quote: hailing from the Early Cretaceous Wessex Formation beds, included in Wealden Group, located in the southwest coast of the Isle of Wight, United Kingdom

facts.statement: Eotyrannus lived in Europe during the Early Cretaceous, approximately 125 to 120 million years ago in the Barremian stage.
facts.quote: que vivió a principios del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 125 y 120 millones de años, en el Barremiense, en Europa

facts.statement: The paleoclimate had a mean annual temperature of 20–25 °C with low seasonal rainfall.
facts.quote: with a mean annual temperature of 20–25 °C with low seasonal rainfall

facts.statement: The holotype specimen measures up to 4.5 meters in length, though it represents a subadult rather than an adult.
facts.quote: Although the specimen itself measures up to 4.5 m in length, it doesn't represent the size of an adult

facts.statement: Eotyrannus likely fed on contemporary mammals such as Yaverlestes and Eobaatar.
facts.quote: There were many contemporary mammal species which Eotyrannus likely fed on, including the spalacotheriid Yaverlestes and the eobaatarid Eobaatar

facts.statement: In 2024, Andrea Cau recovered Eotyrannus as a sister taxon to Proceratosauridae, distant from Megaraptora.
facts.quote: In 2024, Andrea Cau recovered Eotyrannus as a sister taxon of Proceratosauridae, distant in relation from Megaraptora

facts.statement: Eotyrannus is classified within the family Stokesosauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Stokesosauridae

facts.statement: The discovery of Eotyrannus in Europe questions the purported Asian origin of tyrannosauroids and argues for a more complex biogeography.
facts.quote: The find of this animal in Europe puts in question to the purported Asian origin for these animals along with North American Stokesosaurus and European Aviatyrannis arguing for a more complex biogeography for tyrannosauroids

facts.statement: The exact location of the holotype discovery remains unrevealed to protect the site from erosion and allow for future collection.
facts.quote: The exact location of the discovery of the holotype specimen has not been revealed due to its importance and the possibility of new material to be collected as the coastline recedes

facts.statement: Unique features include a concave notch on the dentary, a hypertrophied gutter-like concavity on the surangular, and a tear-drop shaped cross-section on the ulna and radius.
facts.quote: These include: The rostral end of dentary possessing a concave notch housing the most mesial alveolus and a dorsally-directed prong on the rostromedial margin of the notch, curving lateral furrows on the lateral surface of the dentary, a surangular with a hypertrophied gutter-like concavity near the rostrodorsal border, with the caudal end of the concavity containing foramina that perforate the body of the surangular, a low coronoid process on the surangular with a concave area located caudodorsally, and an ulna and radius with a tear-drop shaped cross-section at the mid-shaft

facts.statement: Eotyrannus was a bipedal hunter about 4 meters long with serrated teeth featuring a D-shaped cutting section and proportionally long tibiae and metatarsals.
facts.quote: Eotyrannus era un cazador bípedo de unos 4 metros de largo que presentaba varios caracteres de tiranosauroide, dientes aserrados con una sección de corte en forma de D, proporcionalmente tibias y metatarsos largos.

facts.statement: Eotyrannus possesses the proportionally longest hands known in any theropod to date.
facts.quote: Sin embargo este animal tiene proporcionalmente las manos más largas conocidas en un terópodo hasta la fecha.

facts.statement: Eotyrannus was discovered in 1996 by amateur fossil collector Gavin Leng on the southwest coast of the Isle of Wight in the Wessex Formation of the Wealden Group in the United Kingdom.
facts.quote: Fue descubierto en 1996 por el recolector de fósiles aficionado Gavin Leng en la costa del sudoeste de la Isla de Wight en la Formación Wessex del Grupo Wealden del Reino Unido.

facts.statement: The discovery was initially just loose teeth, and it was not confirmed as a new genus until a jaw fragment was found.
facts.quote: Hasta la aparición de un fragmento de mandíbula no se confirmó que se trataba de un nuevo género.

facts.statement: Approximately 40% of the total skeleton has been found, which is sufficient to determine it belongs entirely to a new species.
facts.quote: Cerca del 40% del esqueleto total se ha encontrado, bastante para determinarlo como perteneciente enteramente a una nueva especie.

facts.statement: Its name references its famous relative, Tyrannosaurus rex, and means "first tyrant".
facts.quote: Su nombre hace referencia a su pariente más famoso, el Tyrannosaurus rex, y significa "primer tirano".

facts.statement: The nasals of Eotyrannus were fused.
facts.quote: Los nasales estaban fusionados.

facts.statement: Primitive Tyrannosauroidea features such as elongated neck vertebrae, long well-developed arms, and an unornamented dorsal skull surface distinguish it from more advanced tyrannosaurids.
facts.quote: Características primitivas de Tyrannosauroidea como las vértebras alargadas del cuello y los brazos largos y bien desarrollados y la superficie dorsal del cráneo sin ornamentación, lo diferencian de los tiranosáuridos más avanzados.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen disarticulated before fossilization, with no part of the vertebral column preserved in articulation, indicating the individual was immature.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotípico se desarticuló antes de la fosilización, con muchos elementos de su esqueleto dispersos en todo el conjunto: ninguna parte de la columna vertebral se conserva en la articulación y las vértebras que se conservan consisten en arcos neurales y centros separados, lo que significa que el holotipo era individuo inmaduro.

facts.statement: Before a specific fragment was correctly identified as the distal tibia, Eotyrannus was reconstructed with much longer tibiae, influencing early reconstructions of the animal.
facts.quote: Antes de la correcta identificación de este fragmento, Eotyrannus fue reconstruido con tibias mucho más largas, lo que influyó en las reconstrucciones tempranas del animal.

facts.statement: Eotyrannus likely hunted ornithopods such as Hypsilophodon and Iguanodon.
facts.quote: Habría cazado ornitópodos como Hypsilophodon e Iguanodon.

facts.statement: Eotyrannus lived during the Hauterivian to Barremian stages, from 132.6 to 121.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Hauterivian to Barremian (132.6 to 121.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: A recent 2014 analysis by Porfiri et al. found that Eotyrannus is a megaraptorian closely related to taxa like Megaraptor.
facts.quote: Aunque un análisis reciente de Porfiri et al. en 2014, ha encontrado que Eotyrannus es un megaraptoriano estrechamente relacionado con taxones como Megaraptor.

facts.statement: The discovery of this animal in Europe raises interesting questions about the supposed Asian origin of these animals.
facts.quote: El hallazgo de este animal en Europa formula cuestionamientos interesantes al origen asiático supuesto para estos animales.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the large size of the animal signifies early evolution of the trait for this clade or if Eotyrannus developed the trait independently.
facts.quote: aunque el gran tamaño del animal puede significar la evolución temprana de la característica para este clado o que Eotyrannus se desarrolló independientemente.

facts.statement: The discovery of E. lengi corroborates the notion that early tyrannosauroids were gracile with long arms and three fingers on each hand for grasping.
facts.quote: El descubrimiento de E. lengi corrobora la noción de que los tiranosauroides tempranos eran gráciles con largos brazos y tres dedos en cada mano para agarrar cosas
